question: Could you find out the average percentage of the total lifetime sales (LTV) that occur in the first 7 and 30 days after a customer's initial purchase? Also, include the average total lifetime sales (LTV). Please exclude customers with zero lifetime sales. The 7- and 30-day periods should be based on the exact number of hours-minutes-seconds, not calendar days.
sql:
-- Build the full analysis
WITH customer_payments AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        payment_date,
        amount,
        MIN(payment_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) as first_payment_date
    FROM payment
),
customer_metrics AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        SUM(amount) as ltv,
        SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (payment_date - first_payment_date)) / 3600 < 168 THEN amount ELSE 0 END) as sales_7_days,
        SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (payment_date - first_payment_date)) / 3600 < 720 THEN amount ELSE 0 END) as sales_30_days
    FROM customer_payments
    GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT 
    AVG(CASE WHEN ltv > 0 THEN 1.0 * sales_7_days / ltv * 100 ELSE NULL END) as avg_pct_7_days,
    AVG(CASE WHEN ltv > 0 THEN 1.0 * sales_30_days / ltv * 100 ELSE NULL END) as avg_pct_30_days,
    AVG(ltv) as avg_ltv
FROM customer_metrics
WHERE ltv > 0
